findings.title: Chunked body chunk terminator (trailing CRLF) is not validated
findings.evidence:
ChunkedReader accepts any two bytes as the terminator of a chunk instead of requiring CRLF. After a chunk's payload is consumed, __init__ sets self._bytes_to_discard = 2 (line 197) and __call__ later does `data = buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard)` (line 164) followed by `self._bytes_to_discard -= len(data)` (line 167) with no comparison against b"
"; any two bytes are silently discarded and the next chunk-size line is parsed from whatever follows. This code is reached for every message whose framing selects the chunked reader (READERS['chunked'] -> ChunkedReader, populated by _connection.py from Transfer-Encoding: chunked), with attacker-controlled bytes supplied through Connection.receive_data(). Reproduced against this tree: feeding a SERVER connection `GET /one HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

5
AAAAAXX2
45
0

` is accepted and decoded as body b'AAAAA45' even though `XX` is an invalid chunk terminator. A front-end proxy/lb whose chunked parser consumes bytes up to the next CRLF (the pound bug described in GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj) can therefore accept the same byte stream but frame it differently, giving inconsistent request boundaries (request smuggling). The fix in h11 0.15.0/0.16.0 makes _bytes_to_discard a byte string b"
" and raises LocalProtocolError when the consumed bytes differ.
